chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Abi al-'Abbas and others, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
When a group gathers to kill one man, the wali rules that whichever one they wish may be killed, and they do not have the right to kill more than one.
Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “And whoever is killed wrongfully, We have certainly given his heir authority, so let him not exceed limits in killing.”
And if three kill one person, the wali is given the choice of which of the three he wishes to kill, and the other two are liable for two-thirds of the diyah to the heirs of the slain.

So this does not contradict the reports we mentioned earlier, that the heirs of the slain may kill two, or one more than that number, because that is only for them when they pay the diyah of the remainder. This report only addresses one who wants to kill a group for one person without paying the diyah of the rest, and they have no such right. There is nothing in the apparent wording of the report to indicate that if he were to offer the diyah of the remainder, it would not be permissible for him to kill them for him. Since that is not in its apparent meaning, and the earlier reports clarify that, this concise report should be understood in light of those detailed reports. And what further clarifies what we have presented is what he narrated:

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: financial compensation paid for unlawful killing
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ الْمُفَصَّلَةِ: the detailed reports that explain the ruling more fully
key_terms.الْخَبَرَ الْمُجْمَلَ: the concise or general report needing clarification
key_terms.الْعِدَّةُ: a group or number of people acting together
key_terms.الْوَالِي: the legal authority or guardian entitled to decide in the case
key_terms.سُلْطَانًا: legal authority or sanctioned right of retaliation
key_terms.وَرَثَةِ: the heirs of the slain person

ai.seo_question: How does Islamic law treat retaliation when several people kill one person?
ai.summary: This report sets out legal limits in cases where multiple people participate in killing a single victim. It affirms that retaliation must not exceed the bounds set by Allah, and it explains that earlier reports permitting more than one retaliatory killing apply only when the required diyah for the remaining participants is paid.
